//: One release train per contract. Each `component` becomes the git tag prefix, so a release cuts `quoting-v0.2.0` or `policy-v0.1.0` independently and each contract carries its own CHANGELOG. An insurer implementing quoting is never asked to care that the policy contract moved.
//core: `core` holds the schemas every contract shares (money, identifiers, problems, the snapshot envelope, distribution, occupation, the vocabularies). A breaking change there is breaking for every contract that references it, so a core release must be accompanied by a release of each dependent contract. That coupling is a REVIEW responsibility — it is not automated, and an earlier version of this note wrongly said it was. What is automated is `npm run versions`, which asserts every contract's version agrees across version.txt, info.version and this file.
//pre-1.0: bump-minor-pre-major + bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major mirror the convention already in use across our other repositories: while a contract is below 1.0 a breaking change is a minor and a feature is a patch, so 0.x stays honest about being unstable.
